subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw remove, harden, or explicitly accept `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` for network-exposed Control UI deployments?
rationale: The source does not confirm the exact arbitrary-origin POST, but the fallback is a documented security downgrade and changing it affects a shipped config path.

options.title: Harden the fallback
options.body: Keep the break-glass flag but add defense-in-depth checks and focused HTTP/WebSocket tests while preserving critical audit/docs warnings.

options.title: Remove the fallback
options.body: Delete the dangerous mode and add compatibility guidance or doctor handling for existing configs that depended on it.

options.title: Accept current policy
options.body: Leave the operator-selected dangerous mode as-is and treat the existing critical audit/docs warnings as the intended mitigation.

recommendation.title: Harden the fallback
recommendation.body: Keep the break-glass flag but add defense-in-depth checks and focused HTTP/WebSocket tests while preserving critical audit/docs warnings.

likelyOwner.reason: Most central history for introducing and hardening this origin/fallback path points to steipete.
